Judgment
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.
2. The present claim petition was initially decided and dismissed on 21.04.2014 by passing Judgment on merits.
Thereafter, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7044/2014 (MV).

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka vide Order dt:
10.11.2022 has set aside the judgment and award dated 21.04.2014 passed in MVC No.713/2012 and remanded back the matter with a direction to reconsider the claim petition afresh and pass appropriate order in accordance with law after providing reasonable opportunity of hearing to both the parties including adducing fresh evidence if any and it is made clear that, this court has not expressed any opinion regarding the merits of the case.
3.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as follows:
On 01.01.2012 at about 3.00 p.m., he was proceeding on Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-1009 as a pillion rider, at the time of accident, the motorcycle rider was driving the vehicle on the left side of Dodda Halahalli-Sangam road in front of Bendagolu gate, at that time one Autorickshaw KA-42- 5027 came at high speed in a rash an negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner was thrown on the road and sustained severe injuries to his right leg, face and head.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to NIMHANS wherein first aid was done, then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery and spent huge amount towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment etc.
4.
The petitioner was aged about 24 years and he was hale and healthy and was working as Agriculture coolie and was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
Due to the said accident, the petitioner is not in a position to resume to his normal work till today, resulting in loss of present and future earnings.

sentences.text: The Sathanur Police station have registered case in Crime No.2/2021 for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent no.2 is the R.C.owner of Autorickshaw KA-42-5027 and Respondent no.3 is the L.R of R.C owner of Scorpio Car No.KA-51-N-4014
are jointly and severally and vicariously liable to pay the compensation.
5. Notice was issued to the respondents which was served to R-1 and R.2.
RSS advocate appeared for R-1. R-2 remained exparte.

R-1 filed written statement as under;
6.

The brief averments of written statement of respondent No.1 is as under:-
Respondent No.1 has stated that, petition is not maintainable either on facts.
Further stated that he is the R.C.owner of Autorickshaw KA-42-5027 and that the said vehicle has been duly insured with respondent no.1.

Further stated that, the owner of the vehicle has not intimated the alleged accident as provided under Section 134 of M.V.
Act and has not produced related documents as provided under Section 158 of M.V.
Act.
Further stated that the driver of auto was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and further not qualified for holding or obtaining sch driving license.

The respondent no.2 has handed over he possession of the vehicle to the said driver and therefore, has contravened the proviso of M.V. Act and the rules framed there under and have committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, the respondent no.1 is not liable to indemnify the respondent no.2.

Further seeks permission of this court to contest the matter on all grounds available to the insured under section 170 of M.V.Act, if the owner fail to contest the claim in collusion with the petitioner.

Further it has denied the name, address, age,
occupation, monthly income of the petitioner.
He also denied the nature of injuries sustained to the petitioner, medical expenditure incurred and permanent disability if any in this behalf.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is exorbitant and highly disproportionate and without any basis.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. Upon the pleadings of both the parties,my predecessors-in-office has framed following:-
ISSUES 1. Does the petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries arising out of rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-42-5027 on 01.01.2012 at about 3.00 pm as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?

sentences.text: In order to prove his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and in further examination in chief got marked Ex.P.12. in his favour.

He further got examined an Eye Witness as P.W.3.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1, who is the insurer of Autorickshaw KA-42- 5027 got examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and one Doctor was examined as R.W.2 and got marked Ex.R-6 and 7.
9. After hearing entire case, decided and dismissed on 21.04.2014 by passing Judgment on merits.
Thereafter, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7044/2014 (MV).

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka vide Order dt: 10.11.2022 has set aside the judgment and award dated 21.04.2014 passed in MVC No.713/2012 and remanded back the matter with a direction to reconsider the claim petition afresh in the light of observation made by this court and also the tribunal to dispose off the matter within a period of six months from 10.04.2022.
Both parties were given 09.12.2022 as date of appearance before this tribunal.
A direction was given that, it is left open to the claimant to array the Scorpio Owner as well as the insurance company as parties to the proceedings and the matter has to be considered afresh.
10. The file was returned to this court on 28.11.2022.
Case was called on 14.12.2022 and counsel submits that, both parties are informed about the date of appearance.
The petitioner advocate filed I.A under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC to implead the L.Rs of R.C owner of Scorpio Car No.KA-51-N-4014 as respondent no.3.
Notice was issued to proposed R-3 by RPAD which was returned as 'no such addressee' hence, I.A No.4 was filed under Order 5 Rule 20(A) CPC for substituted service by way of paper publication.
Same was allowed and notice was published in Hosadiganta Newspaper.
The paper publication report was published on 22.02.2023 Service held sufficient.

R-3 was called out,
absent and placed exparte.

One M.N advocate filed vakalath for R-1 in the place of RSS advocate.
Case was kept for evidence of both parties if any.
Petitioner advocate filed I.A.No.5 under Order 18 Rule 17 for production of document and reopen the evidence of P.W.1 which was allowed.
He filed further chief examination as additional evidence to his previous chief examination.
One document is produced and marked as Ex.P.12.
He was cross examined in detail.
Petitioner evidence closed.
Respondent advocate submitted that, R.W1 is already examined and Ex.R.1 to R-7 marked.
Hence, no further evidence for respondent.
Written argument filed by advocate for petitioner.
Heard argument of Respondent no.1, who filed two citations in support of his case.

11. Taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal, I answer the above issues as follows: -
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per final order,
for the following:-

the motorcycle rider was driving he vehicle on the left side of Dodda Halahalli-Sangam road in front of Bendagolu gate, at that time one Autorickshaw KA-42- 5027 came at high speed in a rash an negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle.

sentences.text: Due to the impact, the petitioner was thrown on the road and sustained severe injuries to his right leg, face and head.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to NIMHANS wherein first aid was done, then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery and spent huge amount towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment etc.
13.
In order to prove his case petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents in his favour.

The FIR, complaint, Mahazar, charge sheet, wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills,
prescriptions, case sheet, old X-ray, recent X-ray and IMV report marked as Ex.P.8 to 12 respectively.

14. Upon going through these documents, FIR was registered on 01.01.2012 at 07.00 pm whereas,
the accident has occurred on 01.01.2012 at 03.00pm.
There is no delay in filing the complaint which is filed within 4 hrs.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint given by one Babu, who is the driver of Scorpio Car No.KA-51-N-4014.
In h is complaint he has stated that, he along with one Ramesha was going to Kanakapura in the aforesaid Scorpio.

When they reached near Sangama Doddahalli main road, one two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-42- L-1009 which was proceeding in front of his Scorpio was hit by a Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-42-5027 which was driven in a zig-zag manner and after hitting the two wheeler, the same auto came and dashed against this Scorpio.
He has clearly stated that, two riders of motor cycle and three inmates of autorickshaw were injured and he had filed the complaint as there was damages to his Scorpio vehicle.
This goes to show that, the autorickshaw came in a rash and negligent manner and cause the accident which was reported in the FIR immediately.
There was no doubt about the accident at this stage.

The insurance company of autorickshaw has strongly contended that, the autorickshaw never involved in the accident only on the basis of history given in the hospital by some eye witnesses and the injured.
The spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3 also shows three vehicles at the spot.
Ex.P.4 charge sheet is filed against only against the autorickshaw driver Chandramurthy R.N. for the offence under Section 279 and 338 IPC.

Wound certificate Ex.P.5 shows that, the injured were brought to Sanjay Gandhi Accident Hospital, Byrasandra,
Bangalore at 5.45 pm with history of RTA near Elegahalli on Kanakapura to Sangama road.

There is no mention of any vehicle in this wound certificate, but this injured was brought by one Shivamuttu,
who is the brother of present petitioner.
Ex.P.6 is the discharge summary dated 17.01.2012 of Sanjay Gandhi Trauma hospital which shows that, petitioner underwent surgery on 04.01.2012 and he had sustained proximal shaft femur fracture.
15 medical bills are marked as Ex.P.7.
Prescriptions are marked as Ex.P.8.
Outpatient file is marked as Ex.P.9.

In this OP register the alleged history of RTA is written as patient driving two wheeler was hit by a car at Madapura village and this history is denied by petitioner in the cross examination as not stated by him.
X-rays are produced and marked as Ex.P10.
After the matter is remanded back, the petitioner further produced IMV report as Ex.P.12 in which the damages of all the three vehicles are mentioned.

It is found that, all the three vehicles Srinivas.M vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32428647/

sentences.text: The complaint of driver of Scorpio on the basis of which charge sheet is filed has to be taken in consideration as the owner of the autorickshaw nor the driver has challenged the charge sheet nor they have appeared in this case and contested the case.
If at all, the accident was not due to the rashness or negligence of autorickshaw driver he could have contested his MVC case as well as Criminal case.
Only on the basis of some history alleged to be stated by brother of injured, the court cannot brush aside the entire prosecution documents which is not challenged by any of the parties.
The charge is filed against the driver of autorickshaw and not against the driver of Scorpio.
Hence, the contention of insurance company that autorickshaw did not hit the bike, but Scorpio car hit the bike cannot be considered.

Even though, the respondent has summoned one Doctor and Ex,R.1 and R2 marked, the Doctor in his evidence has clearly stated that,
as per Ex.R.6 and R6(a) Puttaraju and Srinivasa were proceeding ina bike at that time, accident occurred between Scorpio and autorickshaw and then Scorpio came and hit the bike.
In the cross examination of R.W.2 he admits that, the name of the person who gave the history is not mentioned in Ex.R.6 and R6(a).

Even the signature of injured Srinivasa is not found in said MLC register hence,
no doubt, the accident was between three vehicles, but there is no complaint by autorickshaw driver as to how the accident occurred.
On the other hand, the Scorpio driver has immediately lodged the complaint stating that, autorickshaw came and hit the Scorpio after hitting the two wheeler.

Hence,
I am of the opinion that, this version of complaint based on which charge sheet is filed has to be taken into consideration and on the basis of prosecution documents Ex.P1 to P.5 and Ex.P.12, the petitioner has proved that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of autorickshaw.
Even in the earlier occasion, before the case was dismissed the autorickshaw owner never appeared and placed exparte.
He has not appeared even after remand and that itself goes to show that, the charge sheet filed against him is not opposed by the R.C owner and the driver.

Hence,
I have answered issue No.1 in Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 : As this court as already held that, accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Autorickshaw KA-42-5027.
Hence, I am of the opinion that respondent no.1 being the insurer and Respondent no.2 being the R.C. owner of Autorickshaw KA-42-5027 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of valid contract between respondent no.1 and 2, respondent no.1 is liable to indemnify the compensation to the petitioner with following:-
:: QUANTUM ::
 (i) Pain and sufferings:
 The petitioner has sustained fracture of right femur, fracture of right temporal bone depressed, tenderness in right knee joint.

Initially he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital and later he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital and was treated as inpatient for 16 days and he under went surgery of closed reduction and internal fixation for fracture of right femur and fracture of temporal bone was treated conservatively and he was advised for follow up treatment.

Hence considering the said fracture and grievousness of the injury, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head Pain and Srinivas.M vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32428647/
6 Sufferings.

sentences.text: (ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has stated that, he has spent Rs.30,000/- for medical expenses.
To prove his contention the petitioner has produced Ex.P.7, 15 medical bills of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma, which shows a total medical bills of Rs.7,400/-.
The medical bills Ex.P.7 having the seal and signature of the hospital.
Hence, entire medical bills are accepted.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for total bill of Rs.7,400/-.
towards Medical Expenses.

(iii) Conveyance, Attendant, Diet food and Miscellaneous expenses:
The petitioner was shifted to NIMHANS hospital and later he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital and was treated as inpatient for 16 days and he under went surgery of closed reduction and internal fixation for fracture of right femur and fracture of temporal bone was treated conservatively and he was advised for follow up treatment.

Hence this Tribunal has granted Rs.1,000/- per day during the inpatient period for total 16 days including food, nourishment, attendant charges in all other cases and in the present case it comes Rs.16,000/- under this head.
(iv) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has contended that he was a Agricultural coolie and was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
To prove this fact, petitioner has not produced any documents nor examined any witness in this regard.
Accident occurred in the year 2012.

Hence,
in the absence of any evidence to prove his monthly income, this Tribunal has taken the revised notional income chart fixed by The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in deciding lok-adalath cases, wherein, the income of any person in the year 2012 is taken as Rs.7,000/- per month.
Since the petitioner himself stated that his income is Rs.6,000/- per month which is less tha n the notional income fixed by the Hon'ble High Court, his income is taken as Rs.6,000/- per month.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires minimum four months rest.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.24,000/- as loss of income during treatment period.
(v) Loss of future income due to permanent disability :
The petitioner got examined a Doctor Dr.Prakashappa T.H as P.W.2, who is a Orthopaedic surgeon at SITO hospital.
He has stated that petitioner has alleged history of RTA on 02.01.2012 and sustained fracture of right femur, fracture of right temporal bone depressed, tenderness in right knee joint.

Initially he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital and later he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital and was treated as inpatient for 16 days and he under went surgery of closed reduction and internal fixation for fracture of right femur and fracture of temporal bone

The doctor has given evidence that there is total 16% disability to right lower limb and 19% disability to the whole body.
The age of the petitioner is shown as 24 years at the time of accident.
The age of the petitioner is shown as 24 years.
On considering the age and fractures sustained by the petitioner the disability of 19% is more as shown by P.W.2.
This tribunal has taken the disability at 7% to whole body.

Hence the loss of income due to disability is calculated as under:-
 Monthly income: = Rs.6,000/-
 Total disability to the limb  as assessed by the doctor 19%

Functional disability to the whole body assessed by the Tribunal 7% Appropriate multiplier: =18 Rs.6,000x12 = Rs.72,000/-
 Rs.72000 x7% = Rs. 5,040/-
 Rs.5,040X18 = Rs.90,720/-
Hence, I hold that petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.90,720/- towards loss of future income due to disability.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:-
Rs.
1. Towards Pain & Sufferings 15,000=00

2 . Medical expenses 7,400=00 3. Conveyance, Attendant charges 16,000=00 & food and nourishment expenses:(Rs.1,000/- x 16 days)
4. Loss of income during treatment 24,000=00 period:
5. Loss of income due to permanent 90,720=00 disability Total 1,53,120=00

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,53,120/-
from the respondent no. 1 and 2 jointly and severally and the respondent no.2 is directed to pay the said compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

Hence,
I answer Issue No.2 in "Partly Affirmative".
16. ISSUE NO.3:-

As per S.171 of the Motor Vehicles Act, where any Claims Tribunal allows a claim for compensation, it can direct that in addition to the amount of compensation simple interest shall be paid at such rate and from such date not earlier than the date of making the claim.

This court has relied upon the recent judgment of Karnataka High Court in MFA NO.2531/2018 C/W Srinivas.M vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32428647/
8 M.F.A.No.905/2018 in the case of Smt.Mahadevamma V/s The divisional Controller, wherein 9%
interest is reduced to 6% p.a. keeping in mind the relevant factors prevailing rate of interest and also to maintain uniformity in the orders.

He also relied upon the Miscellaneous first appeal No.6600/2015 in the case of Jayalakshmi and others V/s The managing Director KSRTC where interest is awarded at 6%
p.a.

sentences.text: The interest is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
It is held that the appellant would be entitled for interest at 6% p.a. on the total amount of compensation.
Hence, keeping this citations as precedent, this Tribunal has awarded interest @t 6% p.a. in all the cases hereinafter.
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% p.a.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is allowed in part with costs against the respondent no.1 and 2 as follows: -

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of a sum of  Rs.1,53,120/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of realization from the respondent nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.

In view of the valid contract of insurance between the respondent no.1 and 2, the respondent no.2 is directed to pay the said compensation amount with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this award.
Out of compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioner, entire amount is ordered to be released as the accident occurred in the year 2012.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The complaint of driver of Scorpio on the basis of which charge sheet is filed has to be taken in consideration as the owner of the autorickshaw nor the driver has challenged the charge sheet nor they have appeared in this case and contested the case.
If at all, the accident was not due to the rashness or negligence of autorickshaw driver he could have contested his MVC case as well as Criminal case.
Only on the basis of some history alleged to be stated by brother of injured, the court cannot brush aside the entire prosecution documents which is not challenged by any of the parties.
The charge is filed against the driver of autorickshaw and not against the driver of Scorpio.
Hence, the contention of insurance company that autorickshaw did not hit the bike, but Scorpio car hit the bike cannot be considered.
Hence considering the said fracture and grievousness of the injury, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head Pain and Srinivas.M vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32428647/

opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of valid contract between respondent no.1 and 2, respondent no.1 is liable to indemnify the compensation to the petitioner with following:-
:: QUANTUM ::
 (i) Pain and sufferings:
 The petitioner has sustained fracture of right femur, fracture of right temporal bone depressed, tenderness in right knee joint.
Functional disability to the whole body assessed by the Tribunal 7% Appropriate multiplier: =18 Rs.6,000x12 = Rs.72,000/-
 Rs.72000 x7% = Rs. 5,040/-
 Rs.5,040X18 = Rs.90,720/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:-
Rs.
1. Towards Pain & Sufferings 15,000=00
The interest is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
It is held that the appellant would be entitled for interest at 6% p.a. on the total amount of compensation.
Hence, keeping this citations as precedent, this Tribunal has awarded interest @t 6% p.a. in all the cases hereinafter.
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% p.a.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is allowed in part with costs against the respondent no.1 and 2 as follows: -
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of a sum of  Rs.1,53,120/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of realization from the respondent nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
In view of the valid contract of insurance between the respondent no.1 and 2, the respondent no.2 is directed to pay the said compensation amount with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this award.
Out of compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioner, entire amount is ordered to be released as the accident occurred in the year 2012.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
